decisions.decision: Committee agreed it is identifying priority capital projects, not formally ranking them numerically.
Consultant and committee converged on treating Town Hall/Ritter as one linked project, plus Marshall Park and the elementary school (Turkey Hill), as three priority project groupings.
Noted possible headroom for a third debt-exclusion project since older debt-excluded projects will be paid off before the new master plan's 10-year horizon, pending finance committee input.
Agreed to remove the recommendation to reduce minimum lot size for agricultural preservation, since the 5-acre threshold is set by the state and the town has no local authority to change it.
Agreed to revise the senior tax relief recommendation to focus on reviewing whether existing eligibility thresholds are set appropriately, rather than creating new relief.

Agreed to soften recommendation language from the town 'providing' marketing/space-advertising for businesses to 'establishing and maintaining a relationship with the Lunenburg Business Association' to support small business marketing.

Agreed to change recommendation language away from 'establish a town fund' for stormwater infrastructure to more neutral wording (e.g., 'managing'), since the town has not decided between a stormwater utility fund or traditional taxation.
Agreed to repeat/reference Turkey Hill specifically under the schools section even though it's already listed under municipal buildings, given it is the top facilities priority.
Set December 10th as the deadline for the committee's last round of comments/feedback to the consultant on the recommendations and implementation table.
Consultant indicated a realistic target of a draft final report by the end of January.
Committee members encouraged each other to attend the Marshall Park facility tour on Saturday, November 15th at 10:30am.

minutes.headline: Committee narrows to three priority capital projects and sets a Dec. 10 deadline for board feedback
minutes.summary: The Master Plan Steering Committee spent most of the meeting reviewing October facility tours of Town Hall, Ritter, and Turkey Hill, then debated how to present capital priorities without formally ranking them, converging on Town Hall/Ritter, Turkey Hill, and Marshall Park as the priority groupings. The consultant walked through feedback from town boards on the draft recommendations and a new implementation table, and the committee set December 10th as the deadline for final comments ahead of a late-January draft report, while also approving several backlogged sets of meeting minutes.

what_happened.line: Committee converged on three priority capital project groupings -- Town Hall/Ritter, Turkey Hill, and Marshall Park -- rather than a formal ranking.
Set December 10 as the deadline for boards to send final feedback on the draft recommendations and implementation table.
Consultant targeted a draft final master plan report for late January.
Dropped a draft recommendation to lower the minimum lot size for agricultural preservation, since that threshold is set by the state, not the town.
Approved several backlogged sets of minutes from earlier meetings, after a dispute over how abstentions count toward a quorum majority.

why_it_matters: The three grouped projects are the ones likely to come back to residents as capital spending or debt-exclusion votes, so this sets what gets asked for, not yet how much.
December 10 is the last open window for any town board -- finance, planning, school committee -- to change recommendation language before it is fixed in the draft report.
Dropping the agricultural lot-size recommendation means the master plan will not ask town meeting to change a threshold the town has no authority to set anyway.
